what: Haṭha doctrine and verses — mudrās, bandhas, khecarī, kumbhakas, the four yogas and four stages — in the expanded southern recensions of the Yoga Upaniṣads.

evidence.detail: Śāṇḍilya 1.23 ≈ Haṭhayogapradīpikā 2.15 (taming breath like lion, elephant, tiger)
Yogakuṇḍalī 2 draws on the Khecarīvidyā; Dhyānabindu and Yogacūḍāmaṇi share verses with the Gorakṣaśataka; the Yogatattva's four yogas and four stages parallel the Dattātreyayogaśāstra
Bouy (1994): the southern Yoga Upaniṣads were expanded from haṭha works, perhaps in the 18th c.; the tradition regards the Upaniṣads as śruti and prior

notes: Texts involved: src:hatha-yoga-pradipika, src:khecarividya, src:goraksasataka, src:dattatreyayogasastra.

what: Verses and doctrine of the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha (seven bhūmikās, vāsanā-kṣaya/manonāśa/tattvajñāna, stopping prāṇa-vibration, the jīvanmukta) shared with the Mahā, Annapūrṇā, Akṣi, Varāha, Muktikā 2, Śāṇḍilya 1.42–53, Sannyāsa 2 and Yājñavalkya.

evidence.detail: shared verses on the stages and on mind
scholars generally take the Upaniṣads to borrow from the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha / Laghu-Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha; the tradition treats the Upaniṣads as the source

what: The fifteen limbs read as knowledge, and the list of obstacles in samādhi, shared between the Aparokṣānubhūti and the Tejobindu.

evidence.detail: Tejobindu 1.15–41 closely parallels the Aparokṣānubhūti's fifteen limbs

what: Advaita verses shared by the Adhyātma Upaniṣad and the Vivekacūḍāmaṇi.
The knower's verses of fulfilment ('kṛtakṛtya'; 'dhanyo 'ham') shared by Avadhūta 9–32 and the close of the Pañcadaśī's chapter 7.

The critique of birth-caste under the title 'Vajrasūcī' ('diamond needle'): a Buddhist Vajrasūcī (attributed to Aśvaghoṣa; in Chinese to Dharmakīrti) and the Vajrasūci Upaniṣad share title and line of argument.

evidence.detail: same title; both question birth, body and learning as marks of the brāhmaṇa
often read as a Vedāntic reworking of the Buddhist text; the tradition holds the Upaniṣad to be śruti

notes: Buddhist lineage placement is uncertain (Aśvaghoṣa or Dharmakīrti); recorded under lin:early-buddhism pending the Buddhist units.

what: The sixteen names of the Kalisantaraṇa, recited in Gauḍīya practice as the mahāmantra (usually with the 'hare kṛṣṇa' half first).

evidence.detail: Gauḍīya teachers regard the Kalisantaraṇa as the śruti source of the mahāmantra

what: The renunciation rite (praiṣa, virajā homa, abandonment of topknot and thread), the kinds of renouncer, the paramahaṃsa ideal and the giving of the great saying at initiation; the four seats of the Maṭhāmnāya.

evidence.detail: Daśanāmī initiation follows the rite described in these texts

what: Triple-staff renunciation keeping topknot and thread (Śāṭyāyanīya), codified in Yādavaprakāśa's Yatidharmasamuccaya and followed by Śrīvaiṣṇava ascetics.

evidence.detail: the Yatidharmasamuccaya cites Upaniṣadic and Dharmaśāstric rules on the renouncer

what: Śrīvidyā mantra, cakra, nityās and inner worship in the Tripurā, Tripurātāpanī, Bhāvanā and Bahvṛca; Śrīvidyā commentators (Bhāskararāya) in turn cite these Upaniṣads as śruti.

evidence.detail: nine yonis, fifteen nityās, Śrīcakra in the body
Bhāskararāya's commentaries on the Tripurā and Bhāvanā

what: The vyūha deities (Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha) in the Triśikhi's element concentrations and the Mudgala's account of Aniruddha.
The Darśana Upaniṣad's ten yamas and niyamas, channels, inner tīrthas and five withdrawals parallel the Yoga Yājñavalkya.
